transcript.content: Hello, thanks for coming in today. What brings you in?

Hi. Thanks. Um, well, I'm here because I just can't seem to shake this feeling that work isn't safe anymore. And... I don't know, I just feel like I'm somehow damaged now. It's like the competent person who got promoted just isn't really there anymore.
What happened at work that made you feel it was no longer safe?

Um, I... I'd rather not go into the exact details of what happened, if that's okay. It was just a really bad incident at the office. I'm sorry, I just... I'm not really ready to talk about the specifics of it yet.
How long ago did the incident at work happen?
It's been about two years and four months. It happened during an overnight deployment... there was a break-in. Everything has just been going on since then.
Since the break-in, have you had unwanted, recurring memories of what happened?

Yeah, I do. Um, certain things just set it off. Like hearing a badge scanner beeping, or heavy footsteps out in the hallway, or... or even just getting a late-night deployment alert on my phone. It can suddenly put me right back in that office. My chest gets really tight, and the image of the guard on the floor just... it just cuts right through whatever I’m doing. It just pops into my head and I can't stop it.
Since the break-in, have you deliberately avoided reminders of what happened, such as the office, overnight deployments, or discussing the incident?

Yes, I definitely avoid them. I've started trading my shifts and, um, pushing back on release windows so I don't have to do the overnight deployments. And if I do have to work, I try to just work from home whenever I can, or I take the side entrance into the building. Walking through that lobby after dark... it just makes me feel like I'm going to come apart. So I do whatever I can to avoid it.
Since the break-in, have you felt unusually watchful or on guard, as if you need to constantly look out for danger?

Yeah, pretty much all the time. Um, whether I'm on the train, or sitting in a meeting, or even just grabbing lunch with my team, I automatically clock the exits. I'm always watching to see who might be standing a little too close to me. And I usually keep one ear tuned to any noises out in the hallway, so... I'm just never really fully present with whatever I'm supposed to be doing.
